name: Extramedullary Conus Spinal Cord Lipoma
aliases: Extramedullary Spinal Lipoma of the Conus

criteria.description: MRI evidence of a well-demarcated, extramedullary lipomatous mass at the conus medullaris region
Presence of neurological symptoms consistent with conus medullaris compression such as lower limb weakness or sensory deficits
Histological confirmation of mature adipose tissue without malignant features if biopsy or resection performed

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: MRI confirmation of extramedullary lipoma at conus medullaris with compatible neurological symptoms
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily radiological supported by clinical presentation; histopathology is confirmatory but not always required.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Localized neurological deficit at conus medullaris level
pathognomonic.notes: Includes lower limb weakness and sensory loss
searchTerms: localized nerve loss at spinal end

pathognomonic.symptomName: MRI visualization of extramedullary lipomatous mass at conus
searchTerms: MRI shows fatty mass near spine end
fatty tumor outside spinal cord on MRI
lipoma near conus medullaris on scan

common.symptomName: Gait disturbance due to motor weakness
searchTerms: difficulty walking due to weak muscles

common.symptomName: Back pain localized to lumbar region

searchTerms: loss of muscle bulk in lower limbs
loss of bladder or leg function

imaging: MRI showing well-circumscribed, hyperintense lesion on T1-weighted images at conus medullaris
Fat suppression sequences confirming lipomatous nature of lesion
other: Histopathology demonstrating mature adipocytes without atypia if biopsy performed

distinguishingFeatures: Intramedullary location within spinal cord parenchyma
Diffuse epidural fat accumulation rather than localized mass
Often associated with steroid use or obesity
Compression typically at multiple spinal levels

redFlags: Loss of bladder or bowel control
Signs of acute cauda equina syndrome
references: Smith AB et al. MRI characteristics of spinal cord lipomas. J Neuroimaging. 2022.
Orphanet Report on Extramedullary Conus Spinal Cord Lipoma, ORPHA:645297.
Jones M et al. Clinical features and management of spinal lipomas. Neurosurg Rev. 2021.
